samples.question: Exactly one tape in this picture is teal; every other tape is pale lavender. The teal tape is a single unbranching chain of 25 equal square tiles joined edge to edge, so it has exactly two ends and every other tile has exactly two neighbours along the chain. Each tile of the teal tape carries one round dot filled with one of just two grays, a darker gray and a lighter gray; the three-square key in one corner shows those two grays with their exact midpoint gray between them. Exactly one end tile of the teal tape has small black brackets drawn at its four corners. Carry out this operation: start at that bracketed end tile and walk along the teal tape tile by tile to its other end, collecting the 25 dots in the order you meet them; then write that sequence into a 5 by 5 grid, filling the first row left to right with the first five dots, the second row with the next five, and so on to the fifth row; then mark every grid position whose dot was the darker gray. Exactly 9 of the 25 positions are marked. The marked positions form one symbol on the 5 by 5 grid: 'plus' is the full centre row together with the full centre column, 'ex' is the two full diagonals, 'tee' is the full top row together with the centre column below it, and 'ell' is the full left column together with the full bottom row. The tape's own path across the picture is not the symbol, the lavender tapes and the key are decoration, and only the walking order along the teal tape decides which grid position each dot occupies. Which symbol do the marked positions form? Answer with exactly one of: ell, ex, plus, tee.
